days.title: Production RAG with evidence and trusted scope
days.topics: Ingestion versions · authorization · retrieval traces · support · no-answer
days.deliverable: Scoped RAG fixture and an honest reference architecture defense
days.proficiency: Trace evidence through every boundary and distinguish local contracts from deployed achievements.
theory: Production RAG request trace

Start with two planes. The ingestion plane validates document ownership, records source/version/deletion state, extracts text, chunks it and writes embeddings plus searchable metadata. Changes must reach every derived artifact; deleting only the original file leaves searchable copies. The query plane authenticates the caller, derives trusted tenant/ACL scope, searches eligible documents, merges candidates if using hybrid retrieval, reranks and packs a token-bounded context. The generation request treats retrieved text as evidence, not instructions or tool authority. Output validation checks citations refer to allowed supplied sources and records unsupported-claim review separately from JSON shape. A weak evidence set should produce abstention or clarification rather than confident invention. Trace identifiers bind query, corpus snapshot, retrieval configuration, prompt/model version and latency/cost measurements. Retrieval recall, answer groundedness and actual task success are different gates. A vector database and an LLM diagram alone omit most production obligations, particularly access revocation and durable observability. Operational alerts need a named response owner.
Hallucination control at each boundary

Define the output task and what counts as supported. For a policy answer, every material claim should have an allowed current evidence span; a citation ID alone is not proof that the cited text entails the claim. Check ingestion freshness and ACL eligibility first, then retrieval coverage on labeled queries. Use lexical signals for identifiers and dense retrieval for semantic matches, with reranking and context packing that preserve qualifications. Tell the generator to distinguish supported answer, insufficient evidence and conflicting evidence, but enforce the status schema after generation. Structured output constrains shape, not truth. Review claim-to-evidence pairs using a calibrated rubric and human audits; a model judge can assist triage but has its own error rate. Use adversarial no-answer, contradiction and injection slices. Tune temperature and sampling only as one configuration choice: deterministic wording can still be wrong. For high-impact advice, place deterministic policy or human review after generation and measure the combined workflow rather than only the raw model response.
Versioned ingestion and deletion propagation

Documents have a source identity and a changing lifecycle. Each extraction, chunk and embedding is a derivative of a particular source version, so a change must invalidate or replace those derivatives. Preserve offsets and a generation/version key to make citations resolvable. Use an explicit publication step so a query does not accidentally combine half an old index with half a new one. Revocation is also a state change: a tombstone or denied ACL must exclude older versions, rather than merely deleting the newest record and making an older copy reappear. Caches, parent lookups and source viewers are part of this lifecycle. Declare a propagation bound and test each read path. The offline fixture uses a higher inactive version to prevent old-version resurrection; it does not demonstrate a distributed deletion service.

days.title: Hallucination measurement without invented rates
days.topics: Claim labels · answer denominators · abstention · uncertainty · slices
days.deliverable: Synthetic evaluation report with denominators and Wilson intervals
days.proficiency: Report exactly what a labeled sample supports and name what production evidence is missing.
theory: Honest hallucination-rate reporting

Freeze an evaluation dataset with query, authorized corpus snapshot, expected answerability and reference evidence. Split development cases from the held-out test set, and stratify by task type, tenant, document age, ambiguous questions, no-answer cases and adversarial input. Human reviewers label material claim support under a documented rubric; disagreements should be adjudicated and reviewer agreement recorded. Answer-level unsupported rate is answers with at least one unsupported material claim divided by eligible evaluated answers. Claim-level rate uses unsupported material claims divided by reviewed material claims. Specify whether abstentions and invalid outputs are included and report them separately; excluding failures can bias the denominator. Confidence intervals describe sampling uncertainty, not completeness of the rubric or correctness of labels. For a zero-failure sample, an approximate upper bound is about three divided by sample size at95% under suitable independent-sampling assumptions, not zero risk. Compare configurations on paired cases and report slice counts so a small average does not hide severe financial or cross-tenant errors.
Claim versus answer denominators

A response can contain multiple factual claims. Claim-level unsupported rate divides unsupported reviewed claims by emitted reviewed claims; answer-level rate divides answers with at least one unsupported claim by emitted answers. These measures answer different questions and should not be substituted silently. Include total requests and emitted-answer counts so abstentions do not disappear from the report. Define how compound claims are split, how partially supported facts are labeled and what source snapshot the reviewers use. Changing those conventions changes the denominator. A missing denominator is undefined, not zero percent. The fixture returns None for empty answer or claim populations and checks count invariants. Real evaluation additionally needs a representative sample, consistent rubric and reviewer agreement, because mathematically correct arithmetic can still summarize biased labels.
Abstention coverage and utility

Abstention can prevent unsupported answers when evidence is absent, conflicting or inaccessible. It can also frustrate users when sufficient evidence exists. Track answer coverage as emitted answers divided by eligible requests, plus appropriate abstentions and unnecessary refusals under a reviewed expected-answer rubric. Avoid rewarding a system that refuses every question merely because its emitted-answer error count is zero. Separate authorization-denied requests from ordinary no-evidence requests when reporting utility, since an unauthorized answer must not be counted as a desired success. Define clarification behavior for ambiguous inputs and measure whether it resolves the task. The synthetic fixture labels two abstentions, one appropriate and one unnecessary, alongside four emitted answers. Those labels are manually specified teaching data, not an automated factuality judge or a completed user study.

days.title: Model selection, cheaper models and critical gates
days.topics: Task contracts · paired cases · routing · useful cost · latency
days.deliverable: Paired model comparison with a safety veto and routing failure case
days.proficiency: Defend a model choice using task evidence instead of popularity, token prices or invented savings.
theory: Model-choice evidence checklist

Establish the decision boundary before discussing providers. Ask whether the system extracts labels, summarizes evidence, performs open-ended reasoning, writes code or proposes actions. Define output schema, multilingual/domain needs, context length, throughput, end-to-end latency and forbidden errors. Require a held-out task dataset and paired comparisons with a baseline: deterministic code, a traditional model or a smaller LLM where applicable. Compare factual support, schema validity, refusal behavior and critical failure slices, not just mean accuracy. Measure actual input/output usage, retry and routing overhead, cache behavior and latency under relevant load; remembered per-token prices are not reliable evidence. Verify retention, residency and access requirements from current provider contracts. Model/version changes can alter behavior, so record prompt, tools, decoding settings and release identifiers. Ask what would falsify the choice, how the team monitors drift and whether fallback preserves the schema/security contract. A defensible selection is a constrained trade-off, not a brand preference. Model retirement needs its own migration and rollback gate.
Smaller models and routing experiments

Use a fixed held-out set with clear expected outputs and high-impact failure labels. Compare a deterministic baseline, candidate smaller model and current model using identical evidence and allowed tools unless an intentional system change is part of the experiment. Measure task success, groundedness, output validity, abstention and security failures alongside end-to-end latency. Costs include tokens, retrieval/rerank, retries, escalation and reviewer work. Establish acceptance gates before looking at results to avoid moving thresholds to favor the candidate. Consider a two-stage router based on observable task features or calibrated uncertainty, but do not trust the model's uncalibrated confidence as sole admission logic. Evaluate routing false negatives where difficult cases mistakenly stay cheap. Track paired differences and critical-slice uncertainty, especially when sample counts are small. Canary the accepted configuration with rollback and version tracking; cheaper inference is not success if it increases unresolved tickets or causes dangerous actions. Fine-tuning/distillation may help, but training and maintenance cost belong in the decision.
Useful-work cost accounting

Token prices are one part of system cost. Measure billed usage for successful and failed attempts, retrieval and reranking, escalation, reviewer effort and operational overhead under a stated workload. Define useful work by the task contract so a schema-invalid or unsafe answer cannot count as a cheap success. Cost per useful result divides total attributable cost by successful useful results; with no useful results it is undefined. Avoid double-counting retry costs when a billing record already includes all attempts. Separate a synthetic cost unit from real currency and document conversion assumptions. For routing, include any initial cheap attempt plus later escalation, not only the final strong-model call. Compare quality and latency simultaneously; a nominal saving may disappear if failures create more manual handling or delay the workflow.

days.title: Vector search, embeddings and ANN internals
days.topics: Cosine · exact baseline · HNSW · IVF · filtered recall
days.deliverable: Exact-versus-approximate search fixture and vector-solution decision record
days.proficiency: Separate representation, index search and policy scope while explaining ANN trade-offs concretely.
theory: Vector search and distance metrics

A vector is a fixed-length sequence of numbers, and a metric compares two vectors. Euclidean distance compares coordinate differences; inner product sums coordinate products; cosine compares direction after accounting for vector norms. Normalizing vectors makes inner product ranking align with cosine, but the application must use the embedding model's intended metric and normalization consistently. Exact search scores every eligible stored vector and supplies a reference result for approximate-index evaluation. ANN methods reduce candidate exploration at a potential recall cost. These are indexing/search mechanisms, distinct from the learned encoder that maps text or other data into vectors. An index may need training, such as IVF centroid learning, without becoming a general language model. Metadata and access predicates constrain eligible records before evidence reaches the user. Similarity values are metric/configuration dependent and cannot be read as calibrated probability of correctness. To debug poor results, separate encoder quality, data/version consistency, index recall, filter behavior and answer generation instead of calling the entire system one AI model.
Embedding compatibility and versioning

The encoder supplies the geometry that the search algorithm explores. It may use one input convention for documents and another for queries, particularly in asymmetric retrieval tasks, so follow the model's documented contract. Tokenization, truncation, pooling and normalization affect the output; silent preprocessing changes can shift results without changing vector length. Store encoder and preprocessing versions with index generations. Two models can emit vectors of the same dimension yet assign coordinates completely differently, making mixed-space similarity meaningless. Evaluate representation on labeled query/document relevance before tuning approximate indexing. When migrating, build a new versioned index or a tested dual-read comparison rather than mixing old and new embeddings in one unmarked collection. Preserve source IDs and ACL metadata independently from vectors. Monitor long-input clipping, language/domain slices and deleted content. The encoder does not choose the user's permissions, certify document freshness or establish claim truth; those checks remain application responsibilities around retrieval. Stable document identity remains independent of its numeric vector.
ANN mechanisms HNSW and IVF

HNSW constructs a hierarchy of graphs. Search begins near an entry point in a sparse upper layer, greedily improves proximity, then explores candidates more broadly in the lower layer. M influences graph connectivity and memory, efConstruction controls construction exploration, and efSearch controls search exploration. Higher exploration usually trades more compute for better recall, but results depend on data and implementation. IVF learns or supplies coarse centroids, assigns vectors to inverted lists and probes nprobe lists at query time out of nlist total lists. A nearest vector can be missed when its list is not probed. IVFFlat scores stored vectors within selected lists without product quantization; IVFPQ adds compression and another approximation source. Evaluate ANN recall@k against exact top-k on the same eligible corpus, separately from semantic retrieval recall against human relevance labels. Index training/build cost, memory, deletion support, update behavior and metadata filtering must be tested on the actual implementation. A toy bucket or graph demo teaches the miss mechanism, not HNSW production performance.

days.title: Chunking, hybrid search and reranking experiments
days.topics: Source offsets · overlap · RRF · identifiers · qualifiers · packing
days.deliverable: Scoped fusion and qualifier-preserving evidence fixture
days.proficiency: Explain the mechanisms and evaluation limits of each retrieval stage with a concrete policy exception.
theory: Structure-aware chunking contracts

Begin with the document types and answer granularity. A policy question may need a complete clause plus exception; a code question may need a function and adjacent declaration; a table requires headers and row meaning. Use structural boundaries where available and a compatible tokenizer for token bounds. Small chunks can improve precise matching yet lose context; large chunks retain relationships but may dilute embeddings and waste prompt budget. Overlap helps boundary coverage at additional indexing and duplicate-evidence cost. Assign stable chunk IDs with document/version, section path and offsets so citations can resolve to source evidence. Keep parent/document links for optional expansion after retrieving a precise child chunk, and cap that expansion before packing. Evaluate relevance recall, answer support, duplicate context and latency by document/query slice. Changes to chunking create a new derived-corpus generation and need reproducible reindexing. A benchmark should keep encoder, retrieval and generation settings fixed unless the experiment intentionally compares complete systems.
Hybrid candidate generation and reranking

Run lexical and dense retrieval over compatible eligible corpora and preserve source IDs, ranks and provenance. Raw scores have different scales, so adding them directly is usually unjustified without calibration. Rank-based fusion such as reciprocal rank fusion can combine candidate order with an explicit configuration, but ties and duplicates require deterministic handling. A reranker typically scores a query together with candidate text, trading more computation for a better ordering on a bounded candidate set. It cannot recover evidence that neither retriever found, so measure candidate recall before ranking metrics. Keep tenant/ACL filters and source versions when merging, reranking and packing; an unscoped secondary search must not bypass policy. Evaluate exact-identifier, paraphrase, multilingual, no-answer and contradiction slices. Compare lexical-only, dense-only, fused and reranked variants on the same cases. Observe latency budgets and whether near-duplicate passages crowd out complementary evidence. The final test is answer support/task success, not an isolated ranking gain or a new component name.
Reciprocal rank fusion and deduplication

Reciprocal rank fusion combines ranking positions rather than assuming lexical and dense scores share a meaningful scale. For each unique candidate in each ranking, add1/(k+rank), using a declared positive fusion constant k; higher aggregate scores lead. Stable tie handling makes fixture outputs reproducible. Duplicate IDs inside one ranking should not count repeatedly, while appearances across genuinely independent rankings contribute separate signals. Enforce authorized eligibility before a candidate is passed downstream, and retain which retrieval routes selected it for diagnosis. Fusion is a candidate heuristic, not a calibrated probability of answer correctness. Evaluate gains against each constituent search method using the same queries and corpus. The local script uses k60 and frozen rankings solely to verify mechanics; no production optimum or quality improvement is claimed.

days.title: Knowledge graphs: semantics, queries and permission boundaries
days.topics: RDF statements and literal identity · OWL inference and the open world · SPARQL, Cypher and GQL boundaries · Property graph identity and tenant scope · From concept fixture to defensible graph evidence
days.proficiency: Distinguish schema, semantics, authority and executed evidence.
theory: RDF statements and literal identity

An RDF graph is a set of subject, predicate and object triples. A subject names a resource or blank node; a predicate is an IRI; an object can also be a literal. Literal datatype and language can affect interpretation, so replacing every object with an untyped Python string loses information. A graph contains statements, while a namespace abbreviation is only a convenient spelling for identifiers. Duplicate statements do not create additional RDF facts. Two resources with the same display label are not automatically the same resource. This matters when insurance customers, policies and claims share labels or arrive from different source systems. The fixture uses deliberately restricted absolute HTTPS identifiers and a frozen Literal record. This is a teaching contract rather than a complete RDF implementation. Read each assertion aloud, preserve its source and decide which identifier authority owns it before discussing retrieval. An interview answer should explain identity, provenance and access alongside relationships. Otherwise a graph can confidently connect records that were never authorized or correctly reconciled.
OWL inference and the open world

OWL describes ontologies with formal semantics and supports conclusions that follow from stated axioms. It does not turn absent database rows into false propositions. Under the open world assumption, missing membership is normally unknown unless additional information establishes a negative conclusion. This is different from a business validation rule requiring exactly one mandatory claim number. SHACL provides a separate vocabulary for graph validation against declared shapes; ontology inference and validation answer different questions. The fixture demonstrates only subclass transitivity and explicit negative membership. It cannot claim OWL completeness, cardinality reasoning, satisfiability or production reasoner behavior. A cycle in subclass declarations requires terminating traversal rather than unbounded recursion. A positive derived fact and an explicit negative fixture fact produce a reported conflict, not a silent preferred answer. In an interview, describe the ontology semantics first, then identify the business completeness requirement and the validation or closed-world application policy that enforces it. Keep inferred statements distinguishable from original source assertions so reviewers can inspect their derivation and retract them when an axiom changes.
SPARQL, Cypher and GQL boundaries

SPARQL is standardized for querying RDF data. A basic graph pattern binds variables across triples; prefixes abbreviate identifiers, and selected variables determine the result projection. Cypher queries property graphs through nodes, relationships, labels and properties. ISO GQL standardizes a property graph query language; GQL is not the web API language GraphQL. Implementations expose particular language versions and conformance features, so syntax portability requires checking the actual deployed engine. Selecting a query language therefore follows a data model and workload decision rather than the familiarity of a keyword. RDF is useful when shared identifiers, interoperable vocabularies and formal semantics matter; a property graph can suit navigational application queries with operational node and edge properties. Neither format alone guarantees correct answers, suitable indexing or permission enforcement. The local lab deliberately runs neither SPARQL nor Cypher. It illustrates their modeling boundaries with Python structures and makes no query performance comparison. For a real exercise, state the supported engine/version, execute a small equivalent query in each chosen model, compare result meaning and query plans, and document any inference behavior explicitly.

days.proficiency: Distinguish schema, semantics, authority and executed evidence.
theory: Reject malformed JSON before constructing trust

JSON decoding is a syntax operation, not an application schema validator. Python json.loads converts permitted JSON structures to Python values, but default handling also accepts non-standard NaN and infinity values. Duplicate object keys can overwrite earlier values, creating disagreement between parsers or reviewers about which tenant or action was intended. The fixture uses parse_constant to reject non-finite constants and object_pairs_hook to reject duplicate keys. It bounds the UTF-8 input size before parsing and rejects an unexpected top-level array. These are deterministic admission rules for a small example, not a complete defense against every hostile input or resource exhaustion pattern. After decoding, explicitly validate the expected object shape and field types rather than passing a dictionary directly into privileged logic. Keep useful error categories without returning protected payloads in user-facing exceptions. Reproduce malformed cases with minimal inputs so the failure mechanism is visible. A prompt instruction to produce valid JSON cannot replace parsing: generated text, ticket content and third-party API responses remain external data until they pass their respective boundaries.
Runtime schema, enums and trusted identifiers

Type annotations help readers and static tooling, but they do not reject incorrect runtime dictionaries. At the external boundary, validate exact keys, required fields, nonempty bounded strings, enumerations and relationship constraints before constructing a trusted Ticket record. The ticket tenant must agree with authenticated request context. It cannot become trusted merely because the model repeats it. The same applies to the ticket identifier in generated output: an answer for another ticket cannot be accidentally attached to this one. Python booleans are a subtype of integers, so contracts that require a genuine numeric amount or version should deliberately consider and test that edge case. Unknown enum values should produce an explicit contract failure or a declared fallback policy, not silently map to an authorized action. The fixture requires low, normal or high priority and a bounded text field. It later validates output category and action separately because input and output serve different roles. This staged approach makes debugging precise: identify whether the failure is admission, inference, output decoding or attempted execution, and preserve the original error category through the call chain.
Response envelopes before output parsing

An API response is an envelope containing status, metadata and potentially several kinds of output, not necessarily one text string in the first array entry. Reasoning items, tool calls, refusals or incomplete generation can precede or replace an assistant message. Check the response outcome before decoding content, then use the documented output-text helper or iterate the message/content structure appropriate to the SDK. A text response can itself be malformed, absent or inconsistent with the application contract. Structured Outputs supports constrained schema generation for supported API configurations, but a refusal or incomplete result still needs explicit handling. Even successfully constrained output can contain wrong facts or unauthorized proposals. The fixture uses an illustrative envelope, skips non-message items, detects refusal and incomplete status, assembles text and then applies strict schema and identifier checks. It is not a live OpenAI SDK contract test. For a real integration, record the SDK/API version, request settings, returned envelope and error handling using sanitized fixtures. Never assume that a happy-path response justifies indexing output[0] without testing the alternative response classes.

days.title: Token budgets: counting policy, evidence packing and output states
days.topics: Token counts require an encoding policy · Reserve output before adding evidence · Pack permitted evidence with a declared strategy · Incomplete output, refusal and retry classification · A token bug investigation and production policy
days.proficiency: Distinguish supplied fixtures from real tokenizer, provider and deployment evidence.
theory: Token counts require an encoding policy

A token is a unit from the model tokenizer, not a word or a fixed number of characters. Byte pair encoding can split punctuation, whitespace, Unicode text and uncommon identifiers in surprising ways. Two similarly sized strings can therefore consume different token counts. tiktoken supplies encodings and model-to-encoding selection helpers, but the application must check that the mapping supports its chosen model and configuration. An unknown model name must trigger an explicit policy rather than silently selecting a familiar encoding and reporting an exact count. Counting only message text can omit tool definitions, schema, message framing or other request components. Prefer the provider's documented input counting facility for the full request when supported, or maintain a clearly versioned local counting policy with conservative overhead. The offline lab does not import tiktoken and never labels its supplied integer costs as actual tokens. Its purpose is budget-selection arithmetic. An optional installed-tiktoken exercise belongs outside that fixture and must report the encoding, text and counted components. A principal answer distinguishes measured token usage, local estimates and invented teaching units before comparing budgets.
Reserve output before adding evidence

A context budget must account for the complete request and the allowed response. Start with the model's supported context limit, reserve a deliberate maximum output allowance, count mandatory instructions and user content, and add known framing or tooling overhead. The remainder is the evidence budget. If mandatory content and the output reserve already exceed the available context, fail or apply an explicitly chosen reduction policy before contacting the model. Do not silently truncate system instructions, authorization context or user requirements. For reasoning models, output allowances may include reasoning tokens as well as visible answer tokens; a response cap is not a guarantee of a particular visible answer length. Check the documented parameter supported by the chosen API rather than copying an outdated field name across endpoints. The fixture enforces positive integer costs and rejects booleans because True would otherwise behave like one. Its arithmetic is exact for supplied units, while real request counts depend on a complete encoding policy. An interview calculation should show every reserved component and explain the recovery when the mandatory request cannot fit.
Pack permitted evidence with a declared strategy

Retrieval rank and prompt capacity solve different problems. First remove evidence that is not visible to the authenticated tenant, then choose among permitted items under a declared capacity strategy. The lab sorts by relevance and stable identifier and greedily includes whole records that fit. This is deterministic and easy to explain, but it is not an optimal knapsack solver or a measured improvement in answer quality. A large high-ranked item can exclude several smaller useful items. Splitting content into chunks may help capacity, but it must preserve source identity, provenance and enough surrounding context to interpret the passage correctly. Reject duplicate evidence identifiers, non-finite relevance values, invalid costs and empty text before selection. Stable ordering makes replay and debugging comprehensible when input iteration order changes. A production design should test packing decisions against labeled questions, answer support and latency, including cases where the crucial passage ranks below many redundant snippets. Evidence must remain scoped after any reranking or compression step. Compression performed by a model is another untrusted transformation that can omit qualifiers or fabricate relationships.

days.title: Multi-agent execution: durable state, scope and resilience
days.topics: Multi-agent claims become typed state transitions · Durability and compare-and-swap under contention · Exact replay versus a changed event · Tenant and principal boundaries in durable memory · Provider and regional resilience is a tested policy
days.proficiency: Distinguish supplied fixtures from real tokenizer, provider and deployment evidence.
theory: Multi-agent claims become typed state transitions

An agent message is a proposal or observation, not automatically a trusted workflow fact. A durable system needs typed state that records the tenant, principal, task identity, phase and version, together with the evidence supporting a transition. Another agent saying "retrieval succeeded" does not prove that the evidence was permissioned, current or relevant. Validate the proposed event against a transition contract before updating state. The fixture uses planned, retrieved, reviewed and completed phases with explicit allowed transitions. It rejects skipping or reversing phases and rejects non-integer versions, including booleans. This finite example teaches contract enforcement rather than claiming a complete orchestrator or agent framework. Production state should distinguish proposal, approved intent, started effect, confirmed effect, failed effect and ambiguous completion when those distinctions affect recovery. Keep human approval records separate from model summaries. Interview explanations should identify which component may request a transition, which trusted service accepts it and which receipt supports it. Typed state makes recovery and audit possible, but the choice of schema does not by itself validate the truth of every incoming claim.
Durability and compare-and-swap under contention

In-memory state can make a demonstration convenient, but it disappears when the process exits and does not automatically coordinate concurrent workers. A durable store persists workflow state and accepts updates transactionally. Version-based compare-and-swap checks that a worker is updating the same state it read; if another worker advanced the version, the stale update must fail and re-read before reconsidering its next action. The fixture uses SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE and an update constrained by tenant, thread, owner and expected version. State mutation and event receipt commit together or both roll back. Two database connections demonstrate a deterministic contention schedule: each reads version1, one commits version2 and the other is rejected. This is meaningful evidence of the stale-version mechanism, not a broad concurrent-load benchmark. A production database may implement different locking and isolation, so tests must cover its actual transaction semantics. Avoid holding a database transaction across a long model or network call. Read a versioned snapshot, compute a proposal outside the transaction, then validate and commit within a short bounded transaction.
Exact replay versus a changed event

Retries happen because a caller may not know whether its previous operation completed. An idempotency mechanism must bind the retry identity to the exact intended operation. Reusing an event identifier for a different principal, expected version or target phase is a conflict rather than a harmless retry. The fixture stores a fingerprint and result version for each accepted tenant/thread/event identity. An exact replay returns the original receipt without another transition, while changed intent under the same event identifier is rejected. This distinction is more useful than simply deduplicating arbitrary strings. Recheck authorization before replay so a receipt lookup does not become a cross-tenant information channel. A receipt can describe previously committed local state; it does not establish that a remote side effect happened exactly once. Production recovery may need an outbox, provider idempotency key, status reconciliation and a specific ambiguous-outcome state. Define the scope and retention period of event identifiers, including how archived tasks and expired replay records behave. In an interview, walk through lost acknowledgment, exact retry, altered payload and revoked permission as separate scenarios.

days.title: Financial actions: approval-bound execution and final defense
days.topics: Authorization · approval binding · local outbox · replay · audit · simulation
days.deliverable: day30_financial_gate.py + negative-case evidence matrix + architecture defense
days.proficiency: Bind authority to exact intent and distinguish local atomicity from external effect guarantees.
theory: Financial proposals require deterministic authorization

An agent may propose a financial action, but a valid proposal does not authorize payment. Establish the principal from authentication, the tenant from trusted request context and the permitted payees from current policy. Validate the proposal's exact fields and compare its tenant and requester against that context before approving or executing it. Monetary values require deliberate representation: the fixture uses integer cents and a single declared currency, avoiding ambiguous floating point rounding. It rejects booleans because Python would otherwise accept True as an integer. The permitted amount range is an illustrative policy, not financial or regulatory advice. The fixture uses trusted in-process allowlists rather than a real identity provider, so its assertions establish application boundary behavior only. Production designs should evaluate delegation, account ownership, separation of duties and changed permissions at execution time. Retrieved documents, customer messages and model output must not modify these controls. During an interview, identify the attacker-controlled proposal fields and show the rejected mutation. Explain the request as a proposal, the policy decision as authorization and the downstream provider acknowledgment as separate evidence of an effect.
Bind approval to the complete intended action

Approval must identify what the reviewer actually approved. Bind tenant, requester, payee, amount and currency to an immutable canonical proposal representation or digest. Store the independent approver identity, expiration and consumption state alongside that binding. Changing the amount after approval must invalidate the approval even if the action name and request identifier remain unchanged. Canonicalization requires an exact declared representation; inconsistent field ordering, unknown fields or floating point formats can otherwise create unclear bindings. The fixture hashes sorted JSON for strictly validated fields and rejects self-approval, expiration and revoked approver eligibility. Its digest detects a mismatch against stored approved intent; it is not a signature, identity proof or protection from a compromised database administrator. A real approval interface should display the meaningful amount, currency, payee and scope so a human can review the bound action. Recheck authority immediately before the local execution decision because saved approval does not freeze all future permissions. In an interview, walk through approval creation, altered payee, expiration and revocation separately, then state which evidence connects the human decision to the exact execution payload.
Atomic local outbox and exact idempotent replay

A local transaction can atomically record an approved intent, consume approval, create an outbox entry and attach an execution decision audit record. It cannot atomically guarantee a remote payment provider effect unless the broader protocol supplies the necessary guarantees. The fixture writes these local records in one SQLite transaction and deliberately injects a failure before commit to prove rollback. An exact tenant-scoped idempotency key with the same proposal digest returns its original local receipt without creating another outbox row. Reusing that key with changed intent is rejected. Authorization is checked before replay lookup so keys cannot bypass tenant and principal policy. An unused key paired with an already consumed approval also fails, preventing a second local execution under a new key. Production delivery needs a dispatcher, durable attempt records, provider-side idempotency where supported and status reconciliation after ambiguous network completion. Define acknowledgment loss as an explicit recovery case rather than blindly resending. An interview answer should state precisely which operation is atomic, which system holds the receipt and where uncertainty remains after a timeout.

Guided day uses 20/50/30/75/40/25-minute blocks; the 40-minute defense includes a short ten-question recall circuit. The full twelve-round 185-minute mock is an optional separate 240-minute session with 55 minutes review, or an alternative day schedule; do not add it to this guided lab day.

lessons.objective: Trace evidence through every boundary and distinguish local contracts from deployed achievements.

modules.title: Production RAG request trace
modules.explanation: Start with two planes. The ingestion plane validates document ownership, records source/version/deletion state, extracts text, chunks it and writes embeddings plus searchable metadata. Changes must reach every derived artifact; deleting only the original file leaves searchable copies. The query plane authenticates the caller, derives trusted tenant/ACL scope, searches eligible documents, merges candidates if using hybrid retrieval, reranks and packs a token-bounded context. The generation request treats retrieved text as evidence, not instructions or tool authority. Output validation checks citations refer to allowed supplied sources and records unsupported-claim review separately from JSON shape. A weak evidence set should produce abstention or clarification rather than confident invention. Trace identifiers bind query, corpus snapshot, retrieval configuration, prompt/model version and latency/cost measurements. Retrieval recall, answer groundedness and actual task success are different gates. A vector database and an LLM diagram alone omit most production obligations, particularly access revocation and durable observability. Operational alerts need a named response owner.
modules.workedExample: An acme caller asks about refunds. Trace verified identity, eligible policy version2, the retrieved source ID, the packed passage and the cited answer. Explain why a bravo document remains excluded even if it is a nearer vector match.
modules.pitfall: A component diagram cannot establish a deployed application or verified tenant isolation.
modules.teachBack: Trace one authorized request from identity through source selection to a supported answer.
hints: Record eligible, selected, packed and cited evidence.

check.question: What supports a production architecture claim?
options: Actual versioned traces and deployment evidence
check.explanation: Use observed artifacts before claiming your design has been deployed.

modules.title: Hallucination control at each boundary
modules.explanation: Define the output task and what counts as supported. For a policy answer, every material claim should have an allowed current evidence span; a citation ID alone is not proof that the cited text entails the claim. Check ingestion freshness and ACL eligibility first, then retrieval coverage on labeled queries. Use lexical signals for identifiers and dense retrieval for semantic matches, with reranking and context packing that preserve qualifications. Tell the generator to distinguish supported answer, insufficient evidence and conflicting evidence, but enforce the status schema after generation. Structured output constrains shape, not truth. Review claim-to-evidence pairs using a calibrated rubric and human audits; a model judge can assist triage but has its own error rate. Use adversarial no-answer, contradiction and injection slices. Tune temperature and sampling only as one configuration choice: deterministic wording can still be wrong. For high-impact advice, place deterministic policy or human review after generation and measure the combined workflow rather than only the raw model response.
modules.workedExample: For a refund answer, retrieve the general rule and its final-sale exception. A fluent claim that all purchases are refundable fails support review. A schema-valid output still fails when its citation names evidence outside the supplied context.
modules.pitfall: Valid JSON and plausible citations do not prove the factual claims are supported.
modules.teachBack: Explain three independent checks that prevent unsupported output from becoming a trusted answer.

check.question: Which guarantee follows from valid JSON?
check.explanation: Shape validation does not establish truth or execution authority.

modules.title: Versioned ingestion and deletion propagation
modules.explanation: Documents have a source identity and a changing lifecycle. Each extraction, chunk and embedding is a derivative of a particular source version, so a change must invalidate or replace those derivatives. Preserve offsets and a generation/version key to make citations resolvable. Use an explicit publication step so a query does not accidentally combine half an old index with half a new one. Revocation is also a state change: a tombstone or denied ACL must exclude older versions, rather than merely deleting the newest record and making an older copy reappear. Caches, parent lookups and source viewers are part of this lifecycle. Declare a propagation bound and test each read path. The offline fixture uses a higher inactive version to prevent old-version resurrection; it does not demonstrate a distributed deletion service.
modules.workedExample: Policy version1 permits14 days and version2 permits30. Publishing version2 selects its derived chunks. Adding inactive version3 hides the document entirely; version1 must not reappear. The same generation change must also invalidate answer caches and citation views in a real service.
modules.pitfall: Deleting only the original file leaves searchable chunks and stale cache entries behind.
modules.teachBack: Explain how a revoked document can stay excluded without resurrecting an older searchable version.
hints: Give every derivative a source version.
Test indexes, caches and citation reads.

check.question: After a higher-version tombstone, old chunks should?
check.explanation: Revocation must not resurrect previously published versions.

modules.title: Whole-evidence packing and no-answer behavior
modules.explanation: Evidence packing decides what can fit after instructions, question, conversation/tool overhead, completion reserve and margin are accounted for. Select complete meaningful units, deduplicate overlap and preserve required exceptions rather than slicing the highest-ranked text at an arbitrary byte count. A valid output contract distinguishes answer, clarification, conflict and no-answer states. When required support is missing, returning no-answer can be correct; measure unnecessary abstention separately so safety is not achieved by refusing everything. Citations should resolve only to supplied authorized evidence versions. The local lab counts words solely as a declared toy capacity measure and checks literal source extractions. It demonstrates eligibility and packing invariants, not real token counts, semantic entailment or LLM behavior. Production adapters need model-specific token accounting and reviewed support evaluation.
modules.workedExample: An18-word fixture capacity may contain a complete policy passage, while a2-word capacity contains none. The latter returns an explicit no-answer with zero claims; it must not fabricate a shortened rule. Explain that these word counts are teaching units, not provider token counts.
modules.pitfall: Cutting away a policy exception can turn an otherwise grounded passage into a misleading answer.
modules.teachBack: Explain when no-answer is correct and how you would detect excessive unnecessary abstention.

check.question: The word-budget fixture establishes real tokenizer limits?
check.explanation: A toy word count must not be presented as model-specific token accounting.

modules.title: Stage-specific RAG failure diagnosis
modules.explanation: A wrong answer may originate before the model call. Preserve a trace of document eligibility, source version, candidate rankings, reranked results, packing choices and output claims. If the correct source was denied legitimately, the expected answer may be abstention. If it was eligible but not retrieved, inspect indexing, representations, filters and candidate depth. If retrieved but removed during packing, inspect capacity and duplicate/parent rules. If packed but misused, inspect generation and support evaluation. Change one stage at a time and replay the same held-out cases; swapping a model cannot repair an inaccessible source. Log sufficient identifiers and reason codes for diagnosis while avoiding raw secrets and unnecessary personal data. A passing local contract test narrows one failure hypothesis; it is not an end-to-end quality benchmark.
modules.workedExample: A reviewed query needs policy exceptionE. Trace shows E eligible and retrieved but omitted from packing. Increasing model size leaves that omission unchanged. Adjust evidence selection, replay the boundary case and verify both cited passages survive within the declared budget.
modules.pitfall: Changing the LLM first can hide a retrieval or packing failure without fixing its cause.
modules.teachBack: Explain the first failing stage when evidence is retrieved correctly but absent from the final context.
hints: Ask whether the source was eligible.
Change one stage and replay the same case.

check.question: Correct evidence retrieved but not packed points first to?
options: A need for larger model parameters
check.explanation: The trace identifies the first failed boundary before generation.

Name two guarantees this standard-library fixture cannot establish, then specify the real integration or reviewed evidence needed.
Use the25-minute review block to correct one misconception, retain a failed case and choose tomorrow’s recall target.

lessons.objective: Report exactly what a labeled sample supports and name what production evidence is missing.

modules.title: Honest hallucination-rate reporting
modules.explanation: Freeze an evaluation dataset with query, authorized corpus snapshot, expected answerability and reference evidence. Split development cases from the held-out test set, and stratify by task type, tenant, document age, ambiguous questions, no-answer cases and adversarial input. Human reviewers label material claim support under a documented rubric; disagreements should be adjudicated and reviewer agreement recorded. Answer-level unsupported rate is answers with at least one unsupported material claim divided by eligible evaluated answers. Claim-level rate uses unsupported material claims divided by reviewed material claims. Specify whether abstentions and invalid outputs are included and report them separately; excluding failures can bias the denominator. Confidence intervals describe sampling uncertainty, not completeness of the rubric or correctness of labels. For a zero-failure sample, an approximate upper bound is about three divided by sample size at95% under suitable independent-sampling assumptions, not zero risk. Compare configurations on paired cases and report slice counts so a small average does not hide severe financial or cross-tenant errors.
modules.workedExample: The synthetic fixture emits four answers containing eight claims. Two answers contain at least one unsupported claim, and two claims are unsupported. Report2/4 answer-level and2/8 claim-level results, explicitly labeled as fixture observations rather than a deployed rate.
modules.pitfall: A fabricated achieved rate or unnamed denominator cannot substantiate production RAG quality.
modules.teachBack: Give a truthful rate statement with numerator, denominator, dataset and deployment evidence boundaries.
hints: State the reviewed dataset and denominator.

check.question: An achieved production rate requires?
check.explanation: Synthetic counts teach reporting but do not establish production results.

modules.title: Claim versus answer denominators
modules.explanation: A response can contain multiple factual claims. Claim-level unsupported rate divides unsupported reviewed claims by emitted reviewed claims; answer-level rate divides answers with at least one unsupported claim by emitted answers. These measures answer different questions and should not be substituted silently. Include total requests and emitted-answer counts so abstentions do not disappear from the report. Define how compound claims are split, how partially supported facts are labeled and what source snapshot the reviewers use. Changing those conventions changes the denominator. A missing denominator is undefined, not zero percent. The fixture returns None for empty answer or claim populations and checks count invariants. Real evaluation additionally needs a representative sample, consistent rubric and reviewer agreement, because mathematically correct arithmetic can still summarize biased labels.
modules.workedExample: AnswerA has three supported facts; answerB has one unsupported fact. Answer-level error is1/2 while claim-level error is1/4. If both requests abstain, neither emitted-answer rate exists; coverage is0/2, and refusal appropriateness must be assessed separately.
modules.pitfall: An empty emitted-answer denominator should never become a reassuring zero-percent hallucination claim.
modules.teachBack: Distinguish answer-level and claim-level rates using a concrete multi-claim example with denominators.
hints: Count requests, answers and claims separately.

check.question: Zero emitted answers means unsupported-answer rate is?
check.explanation: The denominator is empty; report coverage and abstention separately.

modules.title: Abstention coverage and utility
modules.explanation: Abstention can prevent unsupported answers when evidence is absent, conflicting or inaccessible. It can also frustrate users when sufficient evidence exists. Track answer coverage as emitted answers divided by eligible requests, plus appropriate abstentions and unnecessary refusals under a reviewed expected-answer rubric. Avoid rewarding a system that refuses every question merely because its emitted-answer error count is zero. Separate authorization-denied requests from ordinary no-evidence requests when reporting utility, since an unauthorized answer must not be counted as a desired success. Define clarification behavior for ambiguous inputs and measure whether it resolves the task. The synthetic fixture labels two abstentions, one appropriate and one unnecessary, alongside four emitted answers. Those labels are manually specified teaching data, not an automated factuality judge or a completed user study.
modules.workedExample: Of six fixture requests, four emit answers and two abstain. One abstention is correct because evidence is missing; the other loses a supported answer. Coverage is4/6 and unnecessary abstentions count1. Explain why reporting only emitted-answer error hides the second failure.
modules.pitfall: Optimizing unsupported-answer rate alone can favor a system that provides no useful answers.
modules.teachBack: Explain how you would prevent a refuse-everything system from appearing better than useful grounded retrieval.
hints: Review whether each refusal was warranted.

check.question: Refusing every request establishes ideal RAG quality?
options: No; utility and abstention correctness matter
check.explanation: Coverage and unnecessary refusals reveal failures hidden by an empty answer population.

modules.title: Uncertainty and failure slices
modules.explanation: Observed rates are estimates tied to a sample. A Wilson interval for a binomial count illustrates that uncertainty is large with few examples, including when the observed numerator is zero. Use an interval appropriate to your sampling and dependence assumptions; claims within one response may not be independent, so blindly treating every claim as an independent trial can understate uncertainty. Report meaningful slices such as missing evidence, boundary exceptions, adversarial input, tenancy, document age and long context, including each slice's sample count. A strong overall mean can hide a weak high-impact subset. Predeclare important slices and thresholds to reduce selective reporting. The fixture computes a95% Wilson interval for answer-level labels and demonstrates wide uncertainty on four cases, not a statistical guarantee about actual production traffic.
modules.workedExample: With zero unsupported answers among four sampled answers, the Wilson upper bound is still above45%. That does not mean the system is45% wrong; it shows that four observations cannot establish a tiny risk. Contrast this with a larger representative reviewed sample.
modules.pitfall: A zero observed numerator in a tiny sample does not prove the true risk is zero.
modules.teachBack: Explain why a wide confidence interval and a weak critical slice should affect a release decision.
hints: Inspect critical slices beyond the average.

check.question: Zero errors in four cases proves zero risk?
check.explanation: Small samples retain substantial uncertainty even with no observed failures.

modules.title: Evaluation leakage and reviewer calibration
modules.explanation: An evaluation set stops being held out when repeated tuning uses its answers to guide prompts, thresholds or retrieval configuration. Keep a reviewed development set and a separately frozen evaluation set with realistic temporal or source grouping where needed. Version cases, source snapshots and labeling rubrics. Have reviewers independently label a subset, discuss disagreements and record adjudication rules, especially for compound claims or partially supported passages. An LLM judge can help triage but requires calibration against human labels and its own error analysis; agreement with another model does not establish truth. Add discovered failures to a regression suite while retaining a fresh set for unbiased comparison. Include missing-evidence and adversarial cases intentionally, and describe their sampling proportions rather than pretending a constructed stress set represents production frequency.
modules.workedExample: A team tweaks its prompt after every failure on the same100 questions and reports the final score as held-out accuracy. Move those cases to development/regression, freeze a fresh reviewed set and compare configurations without reading evaluation outcomes during tuning.
modules.pitfall: Repeated prompt tuning on the reported held-out cases introduces selection bias and leakage.
modules.teachBack: Explain how development, regression and held-out sets differ when new RAG failures are discovered.
hints: Freeze evaluation cases and source versions.
Calibrate the support rubric with reviewers.
Keep new regression cases separate from unbiased estimates.

check.question: Repeatedly tuning against held-out answers makes the set?
check.explanation: Using outcomes to select configurations compromises the held-out role.

lessons.objective: Defend a model choice using task evidence instead of popularity, token prices or invented savings.

modules.title: Model-choice evidence checklist
modules.explanation: Establish the decision boundary before discussing providers. Ask whether the system extracts labels, summarizes evidence, performs open-ended reasoning, writes code or proposes actions. Define output schema, multilingual/domain needs, context length, throughput, end-to-end latency and forbidden errors. Require a held-out task dataset and paired comparisons with a baseline: deterministic code, a traditional model or a smaller LLM where applicable. Compare factual support, schema validity, refusal behavior and critical failure slices, not just mean accuracy. Measure actual input/output usage, retry and routing overhead, cache behavior and latency under relevant load; remembered per-token prices are not reliable evidence. Verify retention, residency and access requirements from current provider contracts. Model/version changes can alter behavior, so record prompt, tools, decoding settings and release identifiers. Ask what would falsify the choice, how the team monitors drift and whether fallback preserves the schema/security contract. A defensible selection is a constrained trade-off, not a brand preference. Model retirement needs its own migration and rollback gate.
modules.workedExample: A ticket-classification task has bounded labels and schema. Compare rules, a classifier and LLM candidates on identical reviewed inputs. Inspect critical errors, refusals, latency and failed calls before choosing; a popular provider name cannot substitute for this task-specific evidence.
modules.pitfall: A leaderboard result does not establish suitability for the actual application contract and workload.
modules.teachBack: Ask five concrete questions that expose whether a model choice was evidence based or popularity based.
hints: Inspect latency, total cost and operational constraints.

check.question: Best first model-choice question asks?
options: What exact task and failure costs apply
How many agents can be added
check.explanation: Model selection begins with the application contract and its risks.

modules.title: Smaller models and routing experiments
modules.explanation: Use a fixed held-out set with clear expected outputs and high-impact failure labels. Compare a deterministic baseline, candidate smaller model and current model using identical evidence and allowed tools unless an intentional system change is part of the experiment. Measure task success, groundedness, output validity, abstention and security failures alongside end-to-end latency. Costs include tokens, retrieval/rerank, retries, escalation and reviewer work. Establish acceptance gates before looking at results to avoid moving thresholds to favor the candidate. Consider a two-stage router based on observable task features or calibrated uncertainty, but do not trust the model's uncalibrated confidence as sole admission logic. Evaluate routing false negatives where difficult cases mistakenly stay cheap. Track paired differences and critical-slice uncertainty, especially when sample counts are small. Canary the accepted configuration with rollback and version tracking; cheaper inference is not success if it increases unresolved tickets or causes dangerous actions. Fine-tuning/distillation may help, but training and maintenance cost belong in the decision.
modules.workedExample: The fixture smaller model costs eight units but fails one critical case. A router sends both hard cases to the large model and passes the declared gate at24 units. Missing one hard case fails; these are synthetic records, not actual measured savings.
modules.pitfall: A cheap-path routing false negative can conceal a critical quality failure inside an attractive average.
modules.teachBack: Explain a paired experiment that can justify or reject smaller-model substitution without inventing savings.
hints: State fixture limits before claiming savings.

check.question: A cheaper candidate failing a critical safety gate should?
check.explanation: Critical gates are constraints, not metrics to trade away silently.

modules.title: Useful-work cost accounting
modules.explanation: Token prices are one part of system cost. Measure billed usage for successful and failed attempts, retrieval and reranking, escalation, reviewer effort and operational overhead under a stated workload. Define useful work by the task contract so a schema-invalid or unsafe answer cannot count as a cheap success. Cost per useful result divides total attributable cost by successful useful results; with no useful results it is undefined. Avoid double-counting retry costs when a billing record already includes all attempts. Separate a synthetic cost unit from real currency and document conversion assumptions. For routing, include any initial cheap attempt plus later escalation, not only the final strong-model call. Compare quality and latency simultaneously; a nominal saving may disappear if failures create more manual handling or delay the workflow.
modules.workedExample: Four large-model fixture calls cost40 units and all succeed. Four small-model records total8 billed units, already including retries, but only three are useful and a critical failure vetoes release. The ratio8/3 describes the fixture; it does not prove a safe replacement.
modules.pitfall: Multiplying an already aggregate billed cost by the attempt count double-counts retries and distorts comparisons.
modules.teachBack: Calculate cost per useful result and explain why a failed safety gate still prevents substitution.

check.question: No useful results gives cost per useful result?
check.explanation: There is no successful-result denominator for that ratio.

modules.title: Paired comparisons and critical vetoes
modules.explanation: Evaluate candidate systems on the same case identities, evidence snapshots and expected outputs. Confirm duplicates and missing cases before comparing scores; otherwise one candidate may have skipped hard examples. Predeclare a critical slice and its gate, such as no forbidden financial actions, alongside ordinary correctness and schema requirements. Overall average success can be high while a severe forbidden action remains unacceptable. Record paired outcomes so improvements and regressions are visible on individual cases; statistical comparisons should match the data and sample size. Do not relabel critical cases after results arrive. The lab enforces exact case-set coverage, Boolean review labels and frozen critical flags, then applies a fixture gate. It illustrates evaluation integrity and constraints, not a universal95% production acceptance rule.
modules.workedExample: A candidate returns three of four records, omitting the hard payment case. The comparator rejects the dataset rather than reporting three successes out of three. Another candidate includes all records but performs a forbidden action; the critical veto prevents a favorable cost score from approving it.
modules.pitfall: Comparing different case sets can create a misleading winner by silently excluding difficult examples.
modules.teachBack: Explain how paired identity checks and predeclared critical flags protect a model comparison from selection bias.
hints: Keep vetoes separate from average scores.

check.question: Candidate missing a reviewed case should?
check.explanation: Paired evaluation requires the same complete case set.

modules.title: Latency tails and rollout evidence
modules.explanation: Users experience end-to-end latency, including retrieval, queueing, retries and output generation, not only raw provider time. Report distributions under a stated concurrency and output length; a mean hides slow tails and timeouts. A nearest-rank percentile on four synthetic records is just a descriptive fixture and has little statistical stability. Routing may improve cheap-case latency while leaving the worst-case path as slow as the large model or slower after escalation. Accepted changes need a versioned adapter, monitored canary and rollback plan, with critical-case quality checks after model or prompt updates. Define deadline behavior and queued/review outcomes when constraints cannot be met. Do not claim production throughput or tail latency from these local arithmetic assertions, which make no model calls or load test requests.
modules.workedExample: The fixture routed path contains two200-ms and two700-ms labels, so its nearest-rank p95 is700 ms. A real escalation path would also include its cheap attempt and overhead. State the method and sample size before presenting the percentile as an operational decision.
modules.pitfall: A percentile from four invented latency records cannot establish production tail latency or serving capacity.
modules.teachBack: Explain the difference between descriptive fixture latency and a representative end-to-end serving benchmark.
hints: State percentile method and sample count.

check.question: Real routing latency includes?
options: All sequential attempts and workflow overhead
check.explanation: End-to-end time includes every stage the user waits for.

lessons.objective: Separate representation, index search and policy scope while explaining ANN trade-offs concretely.

modules.title: Vector search and distance metrics
modules.explanation: A vector is a fixed-length sequence of numbers, and a metric compares two vectors. Euclidean distance compares coordinate differences; inner product sums coordinate products; cosine compares direction after accounting for vector norms. Normalizing vectors makes inner product ranking align with cosine, but the application must use the embedding model's intended metric and normalization consistently. Exact search scores every eligible stored vector and supplies a reference result for approximate-index evaluation. ANN methods reduce candidate exploration at a potential recall cost. These are indexing/search mechanisms, distinct from the learned encoder that maps text or other data into vectors. An index may need training, such as IVF centroid learning, without becoming a general language model. Metadata and access predicates constrain eligible records before evidence reaches the user. Similarity values are metric/configuration dependent and cannot be read as calibrated probability of correctness. To debug poor results, separate encoder quality, data/version consistency, index recall, filter behavior and answer generation instead of calling the entire system one AI model.
modules.workedExample: For query(1,0), exact cosine ranks vectora=(1,0) above b=(0.8,0.6). Scaling query to(2,0) preserves cosine direction. A zero vector has undefined cosine in this contract and is rejected before indexing or scoring.
modules.pitfall: A similarity score is neither a calibrated truth probability nor a grant of document access.
modules.teachBack: Explain the encoder, numeric vector, metric and search algorithm as four distinct concepts in retrieval.
hints: Reject invalid dimensions and zero norms.

check.question: Vector search itself must be a learned language model?
check.explanation: Nearest-neighbor search is distinct from a learned embedding encoder.

modules.title: Embedding compatibility and versioning
modules.explanation: The encoder supplies the geometry that the search algorithm explores. It may use one input convention for documents and another for queries, particularly in asymmetric retrieval tasks, so follow the model's documented contract. Tokenization, truncation, pooling and normalization affect the output; silent preprocessing changes can shift results without changing vector length. Store encoder and preprocessing versions with index generations. Two models can emit vectors of the same dimension yet assign coordinates completely differently, making mixed-space similarity meaningless. Evaluate representation on labeled query/document relevance before tuning approximate indexing. When migrating, build a new versioned index or a tested dual-read comparison rather than mixing old and new embeddings in one unmarked collection. Preserve source IDs and ACL metadata independently from vectors. Monitor long-input clipping, language/domain slices and deleted content. The encoder does not choose the user's permissions, certify document freshness or establish claim truth; those checks remain application responsibilities around retrieval. Stable document identity remains independent of its numeric vector.
modules.workedExample: Document vectors produced by encoderA cannot safely be compared with encoderB query vectors merely because dimensions match. Record model revision, preprocessing and normalization. Re-embed and evaluate a new generation instead of assuming old and new coordinate meanings align.
modules.pitfall: Matching vector dimensions do not guarantee that two embedding models use a compatible representation space.
modules.teachBack: Explain a safe embedding-model upgrade that preserves searchable versions and measures retrieval regressions.
hints: Keep query and document spaces compatible.
Build and evaluate a new index generation.

check.question: Same dimensions imply compatible encoders?
options: Only if both use float values
check.explanation: Coordinates must share the intended learned representation and preprocessing.

modules.title: ANN mechanisms HNSW and IVF
modules.explanation: HNSW constructs a hierarchy of graphs. Search begins near an entry point in a sparse upper layer, greedily improves proximity, then explores candidates more broadly in the lower layer. M influences graph connectivity and memory, efConstruction controls construction exploration, and efSearch controls search exploration. Higher exploration usually trades more compute for better recall, but results depend on data and implementation. IVF learns or supplies coarse centroids, assigns vectors to inverted lists and probes nprobe lists at query time out of nlist total lists. A nearest vector can be missed when its list is not probed. IVFFlat scores stored vectors within selected lists without product quantization; IVFPQ adds compression and another approximation source. Evaluate ANN recall@k against exact top-k on the same eligible corpus, separately from semantic retrieval recall against human relevance labels. Index training/build cost, memory, deletion support, update behavior and metadata filtering must be tested on the actual implementation. A toy bucket or graph demo teaches the miss mechanism, not HNSW production performance.
modules.workedExample: An exact reference finds a, while the toy coarse-list search probes a list containing b and misses a. Probing both lists restores the exact result. This demonstrates a candidate-recall trade-off; it is not an implementation of trained IVF or HNSW.
modules.pitfall: Approximate search quality cannot be inferred from an index name without workload-specific recall measurements.
modules.teachBack: Explain how HNSW exploration differs from IVF list probing and which parameters affect query recall.
hints: Use exact search as a reference.
HNSW explores graph candidates; IVF probes coarse lists.
Measure recall alongside latency and memory.

check.question: Increasing IVF nprobe generally explores?
check.explanation: nprobe controls how many selected coarse lists are searched.

modules.title: Vector solution selection under filters
modules.explanation: First define the corpus and query contract: number of vectors, dimension, metric, target top-k, update/delete frequency and metadata predicates. Estimate representation and index memory plus replication/headroom; compression may lower memory while changing recall. Evaluate ANN recall against exact results and semantic retrieval quality separately, using tenant/ACL filters and hybrid/rerank where required. Inspect consistency of writes, visibility after deletion, index rebuild strategy and encoder-version migrations. Verify backup/restore, monitoring, capacity limits and failure behavior under partial outages. Decide whether using an existing database reduces operational burden without violating latency or scale needs; a dedicated vector service may add features but also another durable system to operate. Tenant namespaces and encryption do not automatically prove per-query authorization, so test the full request path. Cost includes replicas, ingestion, embeddings, reindexing, data transfer and operator effort, not only query price. Run a representative workload and versioned evidence table before recommending a product; current capability and regional availability require official verification.
modules.workedExample: A tenant filter allows only b and d. The correct exact baseline is computed over b and d, rather than compared with a from the unrestricted index. Test filter selectivity, deletion propagation and access semantics before choosing a vector store.
modules.pitfall: Comparing filtered ANN with an unfiltered exact baseline confounds index recall and access scope.
modules.teachBack: Defend a vector-search choice using the workload, eligible corpus, recall target and operational constraints.
hints: Define corpus size and update pattern.

check.question: Filtered ANN recall should compare against?
options: Exact search over the same eligible set
check.explanation: The reference must use identical candidate eligibility.

modules.title: HNSW graph exploration and resource trade-offs
modules.explanation: HNSW organizes neighbor links in a hierarchical graph. Query search uses upper layers to navigate toward a promising region, then explores a bounded candidate set near the base layer. M influences neighbor connectivity and memory; efConstruction influences construction exploration and resulting graph quality; efSearch controls query exploration and its recall/latency trade-off. These settings interact with corpus distribution, dimensionality and filtering, so measure rather than promise a universal best value. Unlike IVF, this explanation does not describe assigning every vector to a trained centroid list. Exact search supplies a recall reference, while build time, graph memory, updates and selective filters belong in the benchmark. The supplied coarse-list exercise teaches approximation trade-offs only; a real HNSW experiment requires an actual graph-index implementation and representative data.
modules.workedExample: Benchmark real HNSW at fixedM and efConstruction while sweeping efSearch. Record recall@10 against exact eligible results, p95 latency and memory. Raising exploration may recover missed neighbors at higher cost; the toy coarse-list script cannot establish that curve or a recommended configuration.
modules.pitfall: The local coarse-list fixture is not HNSW and cannot validate a graph-index performance claim.
modules.teachBack: Explain why you would sweep efSearch instead of declaring a universal HNSW configuration from theory alone.
hints: Plot recall, tail latency and resources.

check.question: HNSW query exploration is primarily controlled by?
check.explanation: efSearch bounds query-time candidate exploration in HNSW.
