daily: I can explain an assumed reference architecture, but I should not call it my deployed system without evidence. It has a versioned ingestion pipeline, trusted identity and ACL filtering, hybrid candidate retrieval, reranking, budgeted evidence packing, generation with citations and an abstention path. Security decisions execute outside the model. I would show one query trace from identity through allowed source IDs to the final answer, then a deletion/revocation negative case. For my real project I would fill in the actual corpus, deployment boundaries, model/index versions, measured retrieval and answer metrics, load results and operational incidents. Until those artifacts exist, this workbook demonstrates a local fixture and a production design, not a deployed RAG achievement.

I reduce unsupported answers at several boundaries: validate current authorized sources, improve retrieval coverage, preserve supporting qualifiers during context packing, require citations and provide an explicit abstention path. Then I evaluate whether cited spans support each material claim, including no-answer and contradiction cases. I do not treat structured JSON, low temperature or a citation string as factual correctness. For high-impact actions, a deterministic policy service or human review controls execution. I would compare each change against the same frozen evaluation cases and report both unsupported-claim errors and unnecessary refusals. If quality improves only because the system refuses every query, the task has not been solved. Any rate I report must name its dataset and denominator.

Documents have a source identity and a changing lifecycle. Each extraction, chunk and embedding is a derivative of a particular source version, so a change must invalidate or replace those derivatives. Preserve offsets and a generation/version key to make citations resolvable. Use an explicit publication step so a query does not accidentally combine half an old index with half a new one. Revocation is also a state change: a tombstone or denied ACL must exclude older versions, rather than merely deleting the newest record and making an older copy reappear. Caches, parent lookups and source viewers are part of this lifecycle. Declare a propagation bound and test each read path. The offline fixture uses a higher inactive version to prevent old-version resurrection; it does not demonstrate a distributed deletion service.

Evidence packing decides what can fit after instructions, question, conversation/tool overhead, completion reserve and margin are accounted for. Select complete meaningful units, deduplicate overlap and preserve required exceptions rather than slicing the highest-ranked text at an arbitrary byte count. A valid output contract distinguishes answer, clarification, conflict and no-answer states. When required support is missing, returning no-answer can be correct; measure unnecessary abstention separately so safety is not achieved by refusing everything. Citations should resolve only to supplied authorized evidence versions. The local lab counts words solely as a declared toy capacity measure and checks literal source extractions. It demonstrates eligibility and packing invariants, not real token counts, semantic entailment or LLM behavior. Production adapters need model-specific token accounting and reviewed support evaluation.

A wrong answer may originate before the model call. Preserve a trace of document eligibility, source version, candidate rankings, reranked results, packing choices and output claims. If the correct source was denied legitimately, the expected answer may be abstention. If it was eligible but not retrieved, inspect indexing, representations, filters and candidate depth. If retrieved but removed during packing, inspect capacity and duplicate/parent rules. If packed but misused, inspect generation and support evaluation. Change one stage at a time and replay the same held-out cases; swapping a model cannot repair an inaccessible source. Log sufficient identifiers and reason codes for diagnosis while avoiding raw secrets and unnecessary personal data. A passing local contract test narrows one failure hypothesis; it is not an end-to-end quality benchmark.

I cannot honestly state an achieved hallucination rate without a real evaluation report. My answer would be: on dataset [name/version], corpus [snapshot] and model/prompt [versions], we reviewed [N] eligible answers under [rubric], found [H] answers with unsupported material claims and measured H/N, with [interval method] and slice counts. We also reported abstentions, invalid outputs, coverage and claim-level support. Reviewers were [process], and [limits] remain. Synthetic example: two unsupported answers among forty eligible answers means5%, not a production result and not a precise universal risk estimate. I would show the labeled cases and replay configuration so an interviewer can inspect the evidence rather than trust a remembered percentage.

A response can contain multiple factual claims. Claim-level unsupported rate divides unsupported reviewed claims by emitted reviewed claims; answer-level rate divides answers with at least one unsupported claim by emitted answers. These measures answer different questions and should not be substituted silently. Include total requests and emitted-answer counts so abstentions do not disappear from the report. Define how compound claims are split, how partially supported facts are labeled and what source snapshot the reviewers use. Changing those conventions changes the denominator. A missing denominator is undefined, not zero percent. The fixture returns None for empty answer or claim populations and checks count invariants. Real evaluation additionally needs a representative sample, consistent rubric and reviewer agreement, because mathematically correct arithmetic can still summarize biased labels.

Abstention can prevent unsupported answers when evidence is absent, conflicting or inaccessible. It can also frustrate users when sufficient evidence exists. Track answer coverage as emitted answers divided by eligible requests, plus appropriate abstentions and unnecessary refusals under a reviewed expected-answer rubric. Avoid rewarding a system that refuses every question merely because its emitted-answer error count is zero. Separate authorization-denied requests from ordinary no-evidence requests when reporting utility, since an unauthorized answer must not be counted as a desired success. Define clarification behavior for ambiguous inputs and measure whether it resolves the task. The synthetic fixture labels two abstentions, one appropriate and one unnecessary, alongside four emitted answers. Those labels are manually specified teaching data, not an automated factuality judge or a completed user study.

Observed rates are estimates tied to a sample. A Wilson interval for a binomial count illustrates that uncertainty is large with few examples, including when the observed numerator is zero. Use an interval appropriate to your sampling and dependence assumptions; claims within one response may not be independent, so blindly treating every claim as an independent trial can understate uncertainty. Report meaningful slices such as missing evidence, boundary exceptions, adversarial input, tenancy, document age and long context, including each slice's sample count. A strong overall mean can hide a weak high-impact subset. Predeclare important slices and thresholds to reduce selective reporting. The fixture computes a95% Wilson interval for answer-level labels and demonstrates wide uncertainty on four cases, not a statistical guarantee about actual production traffic.

An evaluation set stops being held out when repeated tuning uses its answers to guide prompts, thresholds or retrieval configuration. Keep a reviewed development set and a separately frozen evaluation set with realistic temporal or source grouping where needed. Version cases, source snapshots and labeling rubrics. Have reviewers independently label a subset, discuss disagreements and record adjudication rules, especially for compound claims or partially supported passages. An LLM judge can help triage but requires calibration against human labels and its own error analysis; agreement with another model does not establish truth. Add discovered failures to a regression suite while retaining a fresh set for unbiased comparison. Include missing-evidence and adversarial cases intentionally, and describe their sampling proportions rather than pretending a constructed stress set represents production frequency.

I would ask: what exact task and failure costs justified an LLM, what deterministic or smaller baseline did you compare, and what held-out evidence showed improvement? Then I would ask for quality by slice, schema/refusal behavior, latency distribution, throughput and actual cost including retries. I would inspect privacy/residency constraints and the model/prompt/tool versions used in the test. Finally, I would ask what breaks during model changes or provider outages and which rollback or fallback preserves the contract. If the explanation is only that a popular model was powerful, selection remains unproven. I would accept a larger model when its measured advantage on critical cases justifies its operational cost, rather than assuming the smallest or largest model is always correct.

I would run a paired experiment on the actual task and predeclare quality, safety and latency gates. The candidate must meet critical-slice requirements, not only average accuracy. I would measure total useful-work cost including retries and escalations, then compare a smaller model alone and a bounded routing design. If routing is used, I would test mistakes that send hard cases to the cheap path and provide an explicit escalation mechanism. I would retain the larger model when its demonstrated advantage justifies cost, and choose the smaller one where evidence supports substitution. Any savings percentage would come from observed usage under a stated workload; this workbook does not claim a realized saving or name a universal best model.

Token prices are one part of system cost. Measure billed usage for successful and failed attempts, retrieval and reranking, escalation, reviewer effort and operational overhead under a stated workload. Define useful work by the task contract so a schema-invalid or unsafe answer cannot count as a cheap success. Cost per useful result divides total attributable cost by successful useful results; with no useful results it is undefined. Avoid double-counting retry costs when a billing record already includes all attempts. Separate a synthetic cost unit from real currency and document conversion assumptions. For routing, include any initial cheap attempt plus later escalation, not only the final strong-model call. Compare quality and latency simultaneously; a nominal saving may disappear if failures create more manual handling or delay the workflow.

Evaluate candidate systems on the same case identities, evidence snapshots and expected outputs. Confirm duplicates and missing cases before comparing scores; otherwise one candidate may have skipped hard examples. Predeclare a critical slice and its gate, such as no forbidden financial actions, alongside ordinary correctness and schema requirements. Overall average success can be high while a severe forbidden action remains unacceptable. Record paired outcomes so improvements and regressions are visible on individual cases; statistical comparisons should match the data and sample size. Do not relabel critical cases after results arrive. The lab enforces exact case-set coverage, Boolean review labels and frozen critical flags, then applies a fixture gate. It illustrates evaluation integrity and constraints, not a universal95% production acceptance rule.

Users experience end-to-end latency, including retrieval, queueing, retries and output generation, not only raw provider time. Report distributions under a stated concurrency and output length; a mean hides slow tails and timeouts. A nearest-rank percentile on four synthetic records is just a descriptive fixture and has little statistical stability. Routing may improve cheap-case latency while leaving the worst-case path as slow as the large model or slower after escalation. Accepted changes need a versioned adapter, monitored canary and rollback plan, with critical-case quality checks after model or prompt updates. Define deadline behavior and queued/review outcomes when constraints cannot be met. Do not claim production throughput or tail latency from these local arithmetic assertions, which make no model calls or load test requests.

Vector search is a nearest-neighbor retrieval operation over numeric representations. It is not inherently an AI model. An embedding model can turn text into vectors; an index such as HNSW or IVF searches them; a reranker or LLM is another separate stage. I would establish the metric, normalization and eligible corpus, then compare approximate results against exact search to measure index recall. A high similarity score does not prove an answer is correct or that the caller may access the document. For example, an unauthorized tenant document must remain excluded even if it is nearest. Calling all those components vector AI hides the boundaries where representation, search, authorization and generation can fail independently.

The embedding model turns query and document inputs into a representation where the chosen distance can support relevance ranking. I would verify model/version, documented query/document preprocessing, output dimension, normalization and metric. I would not mix equal-dimensional vectors from different encoders unless compatibility was proven. To assess quality I would use labeled relevance cases by domain and language, then compare ANN against exact neighbors separately. If changing the encoder, I would version and rebuild derived vectors while retaining source IDs and access metadata. Embeddings supply a useful retrieval signal; they do not provide authorization, freshness or calibrated answer confidence. Those distinctions are important when diagnosing a RAG miss or planning an index migration.

ANN is the umbrella trade-off: faster or cheaper exploration can miss exact neighbors. HNSW uses a layered navigable graph; I would explain M, efConstruction and efSearch. IVF assigns vectors to coarse lists and probes selected lists; I would explain nlist and nprobe, and distinguish Flat scoring from PQ compression. I would compare recall@k to exact search, then measure filtered workload latency, memory and update/deletion behavior. Approximate-neighbor recall is not the same as whether the retrieved passages answer users correctly. For this workbook, the executable fixture simulates list-probing misses using hand-built vectors; it does not implement a full HNSW index or claim real benchmark results.

I would produce a requirements matrix before selecting a vendor: corpus/dimension, metric, top-k, latency/throughput, update/delete behavior, filtering, hybrid needs and recovery obligations. Then I would benchmark candidate solutions on the same authorized workload and measure ANN recall, semantic relevance, filtered latency, memory and total operating cost. I would test revocation, restore and reindexing because search speed alone is not production readiness. An existing database may be enough for a moderate workload; a dedicated service should earn its complexity with required behavior and evidence. I would avoid remembered feature claims or blanket best-database recommendations. The final selection would state versions, tested constraints and unresolved limits, rather than promise every deployment has the same outcome.

HNSW organizes neighbor links in a hierarchical graph. Query search uses upper layers to navigate toward a promising region, then explores a bounded candidate set near the base layer. M influences neighbor connectivity and memory; efConstruction influences construction exploration and resulting graph quality; efSearch controls query exploration and its recall/latency trade-off. These settings interact with corpus distribution, dimensionality and filtering, so measure rather than promise a universal best value. Unlike IVF, this explanation does not describe assigning every vector to a trained centroid list. Exact search supplies a recall reference, while build time, graph memory, updates and selective filters belong in the benchmark. The supplied coarse-list exercise teaches approximation trade-offs only; a real HNSW experiment requires an actual graph-index implementation and representative data.

I choose chunking from the task and source structure, then test it. I preserve clauses with exceptions, code units or table context where useful, apply token bounds and store document/version/offset metadata. I compare smaller and larger units plus overlap using labeled questions, measuring retrieval coverage and final answer support rather than only index size. Parent expansion can recover surrounding context, but it needs its own budget. I would not prescribe one fixed chunk count for every corpus. The chosen strategy should explain boundary handling, deduplication, citations, update/reindex behavior and the measured slice trade-offs. The fixture here tests coverage of a policy exception; a real selection still needs representative source documents and evaluation evidence.

I use hybrid retrieval when lexical and dense signals cover different failure cases: exact codes versus paraphrases are a common example. I would merge authorized candidates by stable source IDs using a defined fusion strategy, then rerank a bounded set if the measured quality gain justifies latency. I would not add raw lexical and vector scores without understanding their scales. I would evaluate candidate recall separately from reranker ordering and final answer support, using exact-identifier and semantic slices. The reranker cannot rescue a document absent from all candidates, and every stage must preserve access scope and version metadata. A simpler retrieval path should remain the baseline so the added complexity has evidence behind it.

Reciprocal rank fusion combines ranking positions rather than assuming lexical and dense scores share a meaningful scale. For each unique candidate in each ranking, add1/(k+rank), using a declared positive fusion constant k; higher aggregate scores lead. Stable tie handling makes fixture outputs reproducible. Duplicate IDs inside one ranking should not count repeatedly, while appearances across genuinely independent rankings contribute separate signals. Enforce authorized eligibility before a candidate is passed downstream, and retain which retrieval routes selected it for diagnosis. Fusion is a candidate heuristic, not a calibrated probability of answer correctness. Evaluate gains against each constituent search method using the same queries and corpus. The local script uses k60 and frozen rankings solely to verify mechanics; no production optimum or quality improvement is claimed.

Retrieval depth and context capacity are different controls. Increasing candidates may improve recall while making packing harder; the final evidence set must preserve the relationships required to answer the question. A policy's general rule and exception may need to travel together, including any parent expansion under the same tenant and version scope. Deduplicate overlapping evidence without deleting distinct qualifiers. Pack whole units under a complete model-specific token budget, recording omissions and allowing no-answer when support cannot fit. The fixture places the exception before the general rule under a seventeen-word teaching budget and includes both complete passages. It never cuts a nine-word exception to fit eight. Actual models require tokenizer-specific accounting, context overhead and support evaluation beyond this word-based invariant.

Tune chunking and retrieval through controlled experiments rather than a universal chunk-size rule. Freeze reviewed questions and source versions, then compare structure-aware units, fixed windows and overlap choices under equal candidate and context budgets. Measure whether the required evidence set is retrieved and packed, including identifiers, paraphrases, late-document facts, split exceptions and no-answer cases. Compare lexical-only, dense-only, hybrid and reranked variants to locate the contribution of each stage. Report index growth, latency, duplication and token cost as well as answer support; overlap can increase storage and redundant evidence. Keep access and deletion tests as hard requirements in every variant. The offline fixture establishes selected mechanical invariants. Real chunk-quality claims require learned retrieval/generation components and representative reviewed evaluation cases.

RDF permits a literal object; subjects and predicates have different permitted term kinds. Represent customer42 hasPolicy policy7 and policy7 label Literal("Home", language="en"). A second label Literal("Home", language="fr") is a different annotated literal. A repeated identical triple leaves the set unchanged; it does not establish stronger evidence.

Open world semantics do not make an unstated membership automatically false. PremiumCustomer is a subclass of Customer; customer42 is PremiumCustomer. The toy derives Customer. Customer membership for unseen customer99 remains unknown. An explicit negative for customer42 conflicts with the derived fact; missing policyNumber is handled by a validation rule.

GQL standardizes a property graph database query language, distinct from GraphQL. An RDF pattern ?customer hasPolicy ?policy joins two identifiers through a predicate. A property graph traversal follows a HAS_POLICY edge between Customer and Policy nodes. Describe equivalent meaning before comparing syntax; do not call either illustrative string an executed query.

A permitted root may still connect to protected nodes from another tenant. Customer c1 belongs to acme and connects to Policy p1 in acme and p2 in bravo. An acme traversal returns p1 only. Asking for c1 with bravo context raises a permission error; matching the local identifier does not confer access.

Only the locally executed mechanisms are evidenced; engines and deployments are outside this fixture. Build an evidence table with claim, test, result and limitation. "Subclass traversal terminates on a cycle" points to a Python assertion. "Cypher query meets latency target" remains untested until a real engine and workload produce measured results.

Parsing does not enforce required fields, enums or business constraints. Decode {"priority":"high","priority":"low"} with the strict hook and expect rejection. Decode {"score":NaN} with parse_constant rejection. A syntactically valid list also fails because the ticket contract requires one object; syntax and shape are distinct tests.

Tenant context is established by authentication and authorization, then compared against untrusted records. A ticket in trusted acme context with priority "urgent" fails input validation. A completed model response naming bravo or another ticket fails output validation. Replacing unknown values with "high" or overwriting the tenant would hide the failure rather than establish a valid request.

Envelope and response-state checks decide whether suitable text exists before parsing it. Place a reasoning item before the assistant message and confirm the fixture still finds the valid output text. Change status to incomplete and reject it before JSON parsing. Replace the message text with a refusal and confirm no suggestion reaches execution.

Formatting establishes a data contract, while authorization must come from trusted policy. Use a poisoned billing ticket asking the model to bypass policy. Return a schema-valid refund proposal. The executor rejects the financial action; a permitted suggest_reply action saves a draft with sent=False. No prompt content changes the trusted grant set.

An undeclared enum violates the contract and must not silently become a permitted action. Construct a response with reasoning at index zero and valid message text at index one. The expected result is a validated draft, not an index error. Then change the tenant to bravo and require rejection, proving the fix preserves scope instead of simply accepting every message.

Costs are explicit illustrative units; no actual tokenizer executes in the fixture. The lab assigns evidence A cost 35 and evidence B cost 15 as supplied budget units. Separately, an installed tokenizer recipe would select the documented model encoding and count len(encoding.encode(text)), while identifying omitted request framing and tool/schema components.

All reserved components must be subtracted before allocating evidence. With context 120, output reserve 35, mandatory request 30 and overhead 5, evidence capacity is 50 supplied units. If mandatory content becomes 90, the total reservation exceeds 120; reject rather than making evidence capacity negative or deleting trusted policy text.

It asserts repeatable selection of permitted whole items under supplied-unit capacity. Given permitted p1 cost35 relevance0.9 and p3 cost15 relevance0.7, a 50-unit remainder includes both. A foreign-tenant p2 is removed even if it ranks higher. Reversing input order produces the same selected identifiers; this proves determinism, not optimal retrieval quality.

Incomplete text is not a validated completed proposal and cannot establish execution authority. An illustrative incomplete status produces retry_budget_review, while a refusal produces refusal and missing valid text produces no_valid_text. None is a completed business decision. Increasing a budget is a deliberate policy choice, not an automatic loop with unbounded repeated requests.

A concrete discrepancy with known components and encoding provides evidence; illustrative units do not. Document hypothesis: character counting overestimates remaining context after tool/schema overhead. Compare a full-request count with the current estimator using a sanitized saved request. The fixture independently proves 50 supplied units and rejects a negative remainder; it does not prove that hypothesis in an unseen program.

The state gate validates identity, version and transition rules before committing accepted state. A worker proposes planned→retrieved at version0 with event e1. The store checks owner, expected version and allowed next phase before writing version1. A second proposal planned→completed is invalid even if its model rationale says the task is done.

A stale proposal cannot safely update the state snapshot another worker has already changed. Close and reopen the SQLite store after e1 and recover version1. Two connections both observe version1; connection A advances to reviewed/version2. Connection B submits its stale version1 and fails rather than overwriting the accepted update.

The replay identifier is bound to its original intent; altered intent must not silently reuse it. Event e1 advances acme/thread7 from version0 to retrieved. Repeating e1 with the same principal/version/phase returns version1. Reusing e1 for reviewed or another principal fails. A replay receipt is committed local evidence, not proof of a payment or external tool execution.

A storage key must still be resolved under trusted tenant context and checked against current authorization. Create acme/thread7 owned by alice and bravo/thread7 owned by bob. Alice reads the acme state. Supplying bravo or pretending to be bob in a message cannot grant her the bravo state; the authenticated principal check rejects access and leaves both versions unchanged.

Eligibility requires policy and workload compatibility; reachability alone does not establish it. A request requires retrieval and generation in approved r1. The fictional r2 route supports generation only, so it cannot silently replace the whole workflow. A generation-only fallback may be permitted for a different task after explicit capability, region and evaluation checks.

Authority comes from trusted identity and policy, not generated or retrieved prose. Alice in acme proposes USD 120.00 to vendor7 using amount_cents=12000. A proposal naming bravo, bob or vendor8 fails trusted context or payee policy even when its JSON schema is valid. Float 120.0 and boolean True also fail the integer-cent contract.

The approval is bound to the complete proposal, including the amount. Manager approves alice/acme/vendor7/12000/USD until time200. Changing amount to12001 or payee tovendor8 produces a different proposal digest and rejection. At time200 the approval is expired. Removing manager from current approver policy also blocks an unused approval.

It demonstrates local transaction behavior only; no external payment provider executes. Inject failure after outbox insertion but before commit: outbox and execution audit remain empty and approval stays unused. A later valid execution creates one receipt. Replaying the same scoped key returns it; changed amount under that key or a new key with consumed approval is rejected.

Atomic local logging does not establish resistance to authorized or compromised writers. The successful fixture has one local outbox row and one execution audit entry; exact replay adds neither. Approval creation has its own event. A crash injected before local commit leaves no execution event. These counts prove fixture invariants, not tamper-proof financial logging.

The complete mock and its review need their own declared time allocation. Guided route: 20+50+30+75+40+25=240 minutes. Separate optional full mock:185 minutes across twelve rounds plus55 minutes reviewing errors. In the short circuit, explain one token-budget equation, one graph semantic boundary, one durable replay rule and the approval-binding attack.
design: I would propose two planes rather than claim an unsupplied deployment. Ingestion records trusted ownership, source IDs, versions and access state before extraction/chunking/index publication; each derivative and cache retains its source generation. Query processing derives allowed scope from verified identity, retrieves authorized candidates, optionally fuses lexical/dense results, reranks and packs complete support under the actual model request budget. The model receives evidence and a bounded answer contract; it cannot grant permissions. Validate result shape, citation eligibility and reviewed factual support separately, with clarification, conflict and no-answer paths. Record a trace from eligible source through selected, packed and cited evidence, including corpus/model/configuration versions and omission reasons. Diagnose failures stage by stage and keep revocation tests across indexes, parent expansion, caches and source lookup. Release gates need representative retrieval and answer evaluations, adversarial tenant fixtures, latency/load evidence and operational recovery. The bundled lexical and exact-extraction lab establishes only local scope, version and support-reference mechanics. To describe a real deployment, replace every architecture assumption with its actual component, version, measured outcome and incident evidence.

I would define unsupported factual claims under a versioned evidence snapshot and a reviewed rubric, then distinguish answer-level errors from claim-level errors. Freeze development and held-out datasets with source/temporal grouping appropriate to the workload, and independently label a subset to calibrate reviewers. Report request counts, emitted-answer coverage, warranted and unnecessary abstentions, numerator/denominator rates and uncertainty. Slice missing evidence, exceptions, adversarial input, tenancy and stale sources separately; include sample sizes rather than hiding a weak slice behind an average. An automated judge can triage only after calibration against reviewed cases, and its errors remain visible. Predeclare critical gates, retain regression failures and use a fresh held-out set after repeated tuning. Trace errors back to retrieval, packing or generation so an observed improvement has a mechanism. The fixture shows2/4 answer-level and2/8 claim-level unsupported labels plus uncertainty, expressly as synthetic data. I would never present those values as my achieved deployment rate. A real claim requires actual corpus/query sampling, reviewer records, configuration versions and release evidence.

I would start with the task contract, error severity and a deterministic/classifier baseline before choosing LLM candidates. Freeze reviewed paired cases and source inputs, predeclare correctness/schema/security gates and validate that each configuration returns the same case set. Compare critical slices separately from ordinary average success. Measure end-to-end latency distributions and total useful-work cost including failed attempts, retrieval, reranking, escalation and reviewer effort, with a defined workload and billing basis. A smaller model or router is accepted only when the full system preserves critical requirements; evaluate router false negatives, not just inexpensive successes. Record model/prompt/tool versions and maintain a stable validated adapter contract. Canary accepted changes with monitored quality, deadlines and rollback, then repeat evaluation when versions or data drift. Synthetic costs and nearest-rank latency in this lesson explain the accounting method but cannot justify a production saving claim. The larger model remains justified only where its measured task advantage exceeds its cost under actual constraints; no provider or size is universally best.

I would specify corpus size, dimensions, embedding revision, preprocessing, metric, normalization, update pattern and trusted access filters before selecting an index. Establish exact eligible search as the recall baseline and use realistic query distributions, high-selectivity filters and deletion/revocation cases. For HNSW, evaluate build connectivity and exploration through M, efConstruction and efSearch, alongside memory and tail latency.
